resources.string: To count, I have to look.

Reelómetro uses Android\'s accessibility service to read the screen of TikTok, Instagram and YouTube while you use them. That way it detects each short video you watch and stores, only on this phone, which app you watched it in, when, for how long, who posted it and its description, so it can show you your statistics.

On TikTok, Instagram and YouTube: when you move on to the next short video and the visible text of that video (the creator\'s name, the description and the hashtags). Also when you tap “Share” and, only on Instagram and if you turn on “Who you send to” in Settings, the name of the person or group you send it to. If you also use quick send, it reads the names on the share sheet to find the person you have pinned.

Anything in other apps: from them it only knows that you have left, so it can stop counting. It does not store what you type or your messages. It only taps for you if you use Instagram quick send, and then only “Share”, the person or group you have pinned and “Send”, by tapping their button; if it can\'t see them, it types their name into the search box on the sheet. Only with quick send does it crop the profile photos of the people or groups you pin from the share sheet, to show them on their button; it keeps them only on this phone and takes no other screenshots.
Only to count how many videos you watch, for how long, on which topics and from which creators. It is not used for advertising or to build profiles.
On this phone and nowhere else. It is not sent to any server or shared with anyone: the app does not even have permission to use the internet.
You can turn off the permission whenever you like in Settings > Accessibility, and delete all the data from within the app.
If you accept, I\'ll take you to Android\'s settings to turn on the permission. If you don\'t, the app won\'t be able to count anything; you can turn it on later from Today or from Settings.
No permission, no count. Whenever you like, it is in Today and in Settings.
